segments.speaker: JOHN
segments.en: Erm ... hello Professor, I’m John Wishart. I’m working on my entry for the Global Design Competition. My tutor said you might be able to help me with it.

segments.speaker: PROFESSOR
segments.en: Ah, yes, I got a copy of your drawings. Come in and tell me about it. What sort of competition is it?

segments.speaker: JOHN
segments.en: Well, it’s an international design competition and we have to come up with a new design for a typical domestic kitchen appliance.

segments.speaker: PROFESSOR
segments.en: I see, and are there any special conditions? Does it have to save energy for example?

segments.speaker: JOHN
segments.en: Actually that was the focus in last year’s competition. This year’s different. We have to adopt an innovative approach to existing technology, using it in a way that hasn’t been thought of before.

segments.speaker: PROFESSOR
segments.en: I see, that sounds tricky. And what kitchen appliance have you chosen?

segments.speaker: JOHN
segments.en: Well, I decided to choose the dishwasher.

segments.speaker: PROFESSOR
segments.en: Interesting, what made you choose that?

segments.speaker: JOHN
segments.en: Well, they’re an everyday kitchen appliance in most Australian houses but they’re all pretty boring and almost identical to each other. I think some people will be prepared to pay a little extra for something that looks different.

segments.speaker: PROFESSOR
segments.en: That’s a nice idea. I see you’ve called your design ‘the Rockpool’; why is that?

segments.speaker: JOHN
segments.en: Basically because it looks like the rock pools you find on a beach. The top is made of glass so that you can look down into it.

segments.speaker: PROFESSOR
segments.en: And there’s a stone at the bottom. Is that just for decoration?

segments.speaker: JOHN
segments.en: Actually it does have a function. Instead of pushing a button, you turn the stone.

segments.speaker: PROFESSOR
segments.en: So it’s really just a novel way of starting the dishwasher.

segments.speaker: JOHN
segments.en: That’s right.

segments.speaker: PROFESSOR
segments.en: It’s a really nice design, but what makes it innovative?

segments.speaker: JOHN
segments.en: Well, I decided to make a dishwasher that uses carbon dioxide.

segments.speaker: PROFESSOR
segments.en: In place of water and detergent? How will you manage that?

segments.speaker: JOHN
segments.en: The idea is to pressurize the carbon dioxide so that it becomes a liquid. The fluid is then released into the dishwasher where it cleans the dishes all by itself.

segments.speaker: PROFESSOR
segments.en: Sounds like a brilliant idea! Your system will totally do away with the need for strong detergents. So what happens once the dishes are clean?

segments.speaker: JOHN
segments.en: Well, to allow them to dry, the liquid carbon dioxide and the waste materials all go to an area called the holding chamber. That’s where the liquid is depressurised and so it reverts to a gas. Then the oil and grease are separated out and sent to the waste system.

segments.speaker: PROFESSOR
segments.en: It sounds like you’ve thought it all out very thoroughly. So, what happens to the carbon dioxide once the process is complete? Not wasted I hope.

segments.speaker: JOHN
segments.en: Actually, that’s where the real savings are made. The carbon dioxide is sent back to the cylinder and can be used again and again.

segments.speaker: PROFESSOR
segments.en: What a terrific idea. Do you think it will ever be built?

segments.speaker: JOHN
segments.en: Probably not, but that’s OK.

segments.speaker: PROFESSOR
segments.en: Well, I’m sure a lot of positive things will come out of your design. ———————————

segments.speaker: PROFESSOR
segments.en: Now, you seem to have thought about everything so what exactly did you need me to help you with?

segments.speaker: JOHN
segments.en: Well, my design has made it to the final stage of the competition and, in a few months’ time, I have to give a presentation, and that’s the part I was hoping you could help me with.

segments.speaker: PROFESSOR
segments.en: Right, well that should be easy enough. What have you managed to do so far?

segments.speaker: JOHN
segments.en: Well, I’ve got detailed drawings to show how it will work and I’ve also written a 500-word paper on it.

segments.speaker: PROFESSOR
segments.en: I see. Well, if you want to stand a good chance of winning you really need a model of the machine.

segments.speaker: JOHN
segments.en: Yes, I thought I might but I’m having a few problems.

segments.speaker: PROFESSOR
segments.en: What is the main difficulty so far? Let me guess – is it the materials?

segments.speaker: JOHN
segments.en: Yes. I want it to look professional but everything that’s top quality is also very expensive.

segments.speaker: PROFESSOR
segments.en: Look, projects like this are very important to us. They really help lift our profile. So why don’t you talk to the university about a grant? I can help you fill out the application forms if you like.

segments.speaker: JOHN
segments.en: That would be great.

segments.speaker: PROFESSOR
segments.en: You’d better show me this paper you’ve written as well. For a global competition such as this you need to make sure the technical details you’ve given are accurate and thorough.

segments.speaker: JOHN
segments.en: That would be a great help.

segments.speaker: PROFESSOR
segments.en: Is there anything else I can do?

segments.speaker: JOHN

SECTION 3
Questions 21-30
GLOBAL DESIGN COMPETITION
Choose the correct letter A, B or C.
Questions:
    Q Num: 21
    Text: Students entering the design competition have to
    Options:
        produce an energy-efficient design.
        adapt an existing energy-saving appliance.
        develop a new use for current technology.
    Q Num: 22
    Text: John chose a dishwasher because he wanted to make dishwashers
    Options:
        more appealing.
        more common.
        more economical.
    Q Num: 23
    Text: The stone in John's 'Rockpool' design is used
    Options:
        for decoration.
        to switch it on.
        to stop water escaping.
    Q Num: 24
    Text: In the holding chamber, the carbon dioxide
    Options:
        changes back to a gas.
        dries the dishes.
        is allowed to cool.
    Q Num: 25
    Text: At the end of the cleaning process, the carbon dioxide
    Options:
        is released into the air.
        is disposed of with the waste.
        is collected ready to be re-used.
Complete the notes below.
Write ONE WORD ONLY for each answer.
